verses.zh: 素来没有访问我的，现在求问我；没有寻找我的，我叫他们遇见；没有称为我名下的，我对他们说：我在这里！我在这里！
verses.en: “I made myself available to those who did not ask for me;[NOTE:1] I appeared to those who did not look for me.[NOTE:2] I said, ‘Here I am! Here I am!’to a nation that did not invoke[NOTE:3] my name.
notes: Heb “I allowed myself to be sought by those who did not ask.”
Heb “I allowed myself to be found by those who did not seek.”
Heb “call out in”; NASB, NIV, NRSV “call on.”

verses.zh: 我整天伸手招呼那悖逆的百姓；他们随自己的意念行不善之道。
verses.en: I spread out my hands all day longto my rebellious people,who lived in a way that is morally unacceptableand who did what they desired.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “who walked [in] the way that is not good, after their thoughts.”

verses.zh: 这百姓时常当面惹我发怒；在园中献祭，在坛（原文是砖）上烧香；
verses.en: These people continually and blatantly offend me[NOTE:1] as they sacrifice in their sacred orchards[NOTE:2] and burn incense on brick altars.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “the people who provoke me to anger to my face continually.”
Or “gardens” (KJV, NASB, NIV, NRSV, NLT).
Or perhaps, “on tiles.”

verses.zh: 在坟墓间坐着，在隐密处住宿，吃猪肉；他们器皿中有可憎之物做的汤；
verses.en: They sit among the tombs[NOTE:1] and keep watch all night long.[NOTE:2] They eat pork[NOTE:3] and broth[NOTE:4] from unclean sacrificial meat is in their pans.
notes: Perhaps the worship of underworld deities or dead spirits is in view.

The Hebrew text reads literally, “and in the watches they spend the night.” Some understand נְּצוּרִים (netsurim) as referring to “secret places” or “caves,” while others emend the text to וּבֵין צוּרִים (uven tsurim, “between the rocky cliffs”).
Heb “the flesh of the pig”; KJV, NAB, NASB “swine’s flesh.”
The marginal reading (Qere), supported by the Qumran scroll 1QIsaa, reads מְרַק (meraq, “broth”), while the consonantal text (Kethib) has פְרַק (feraq, “fragment”).

verses.zh: 且对人说：你站开吧！不要挨近我，因为我比你圣洁。主说：这些人是我鼻中的烟，是整天烧着的火。
verses.en: They say, ‘Keep to yourself!Don’t get near me, for I am holier than you!’These people are like smoke in my nostrils,like a fire that keeps burning all day long.

verses.zh: 看哪，这都写在我面前。我必不静默，必施行报应，必将你们的罪孽和你们列祖的罪孽，就是在山上烧香，在冈上亵渎我的罪孽，一同报应在他们后人怀中，我先要把他们所行的量给他们；这是耶和华说的。
verses.en: Look, I have decreed:[NOTE:1] I will not keep silent, but will pay them back;I will pay them back exactly what they deserve,[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Look, it is written before me.”
Heb “I will pay back into their lap.”

verses.zh: a
verses.en: for your sins and your ancestors’ sins,”[NOTE:1] says the Lord.“Because they burned incense on the mountainsand offended[NOTE:2] me on the hills,I will punish them in full measure.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “the iniquities of your fathers.”
Or perhaps, “taunted”; KJV “blasphemed”; NAB “disgraced”; NASB “scorned”; NIV “defied”; NRSV “reviled.”
Heb “I will measure out their pay [from the] beginning into their lap,” i.e., he will give them everything they have earned.

verses.zh: 耶和华如此说：葡萄中寻得新酒，人就说：不要毁坏，因为福在其中。我因我仆人的缘故也必照样而行，不将他们全然毁灭。
verses.en: This is what the Lord says:“When[NOTE:1] juice is discovered in a cluster of grapes,someone says, ‘Don’t destroy it, for it contains juice.’[NOTE:2] So I will do for the sake of my servants—I will not destroy everyone.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “just as.” In the Hebrew text the statement is one long sentence, “Just as…, so I will do….”
Heb “for a blessing is in it.”
Heb “by not destroying everyone.”

verses.zh: 我必从雅各中领出后裔，从犹大中领出承受我众山的。我的选民必承受；我的仆人要在那里居住。
verses.en: I will bring forth descendants from Jacoband from Judah people to take possession of my mountains.My chosen ones will take possession of the land;[NOTE:1] my servants will live there.
notes: Heb “it.” The third feminine singular pronominal suffix probably refers to the land that contains the aforementioned mountains.

verses.zh: 沙仑平原必成为羊群的圈；亚割谷必成为牛群躺卧之处，都为寻求我的民所得。
verses.en: Sharon[NOTE:1] will become a pasture for sheep,and the Valley of Achor[NOTE:2] a place where cattle graze;[NOTE:3] they will belong to my people, who seek me.[NOTE:4]
notes: Sharon was a plain located to the west, along the Mediterranean coast north of Joppa and south of Carmel.
The Valley of Achor (“Achor” means “trouble” in Hebrew) was the site of Achan’s execution. It was located to the east, near Jericho.
Heb “a resting place for cattle”; NASB, NIV “for herds.”
Heb “for my people who seek me.”

verses.zh: 但你们这些离弃耶和华、忘记我的圣山、给时运摆筵席（原文是桌子）、给天命盛满调和酒的，
verses.en: But as for you who abandon the Lordand forget about worshiping at[NOTE:1] my holy mountain,who prepare a feast for the god called ‘Fortune,’[NOTE:2] and fill up wine jugs for the god called ‘Destiny’[NOTE:3]—
notes: The Hebrew text has simply, “forget.” The words “about worshiping at” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
The Hebrew has לַגַּד (laggad, “for Gad”), the name of a pagan deity. See HALOT 176 s.v. II גַּד 2.
The Hebrew has לַמְנִי (lamni, “for Meni”), the name of a pagan deity. See HALOT 602 s.v. מְגִי.

verses.zh: 我要命定你们归在刀下，都必屈身被杀；因为我呼唤，你们没有答应；我说话，你们没有听从；反倒行我眼中看为恶的，拣选我所不喜悦的。
verses.en: I predestine you to die by the sword,[NOTE:1] all of you will kneel down at the slaughtering block,[NOTE:2] because I called to you, and you did not respond;I spoke and you did not listen.You did evil before me;[NOTE:3] you chose to do what displeases me.”
notes: Heb “I assign you to the sword.” Some emend the Qal verb form מָנִיתִי (maniti, “I assign”) to the Piel מִנִּיתִי (minniti, “ I ordain”). The verb sounds like the name of the god Meni (מְנִי, meni, “Destiny, Fate”). The sound play draws attention to the irony of the statement. The sinners among God’s people worship the god Meni, apparently in an effort to ensure a bright destiny for themselves. But the Lord is the one who really determines their destiny and he has decreed their demise.
Or “at the slaughter”; NIV11 “in the slaughter”; NLT “before the executioner.”
Heb “that which is evil in my eyes.”

verses.zh: 所以，主耶和华如此说：我的仆人必得吃，你们却饥饿；我的仆人必得喝，你们却干渴；我的仆人必欢喜，你们却蒙羞。
verses.en: So this is what the Sovereign Lord says:“Look, my servants will eat, but you will be hungry.Look, my servants will drink, but you will be thirsty.Look, my servants will rejoice, but you will be humiliated.

verses.zh: 我的仆人因心中高兴欢呼，你们却因心中忧愁哀哭，又因心里忧伤哀号。
verses.en: Look, my servants will shout for joy as happiness fills their hearts.[NOTE:1] But you will cry out as sorrow fills your hearts;[NOTE:2] you will wail because your spirits will be crushed.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “from the good of the heart.”
Heb “from the pain of the heart.”
Heb “from the breaking of the spirit.”

verses.zh: 你们必留下自己的名，为我选民指着赌咒。主耶和华必杀你们，另起别名称呼他的仆人。
verses.en: Your names will live on in the curse formulas of my chosen ones.[NOTE:1] The Sovereign Lord will kill you,but he will give his servants another name.
notes: Heb “you will leave your name for an oath to my chosen ones.”sn For an example of such a curse formula see Jer 29:22.

verses.zh: 这样，在地上为自己求福的，必凭真实的　神求福；在地上起誓的，必指真实的　神起誓。因为，从前的患难已经忘记，也从我眼前隐藏了。
verses.en: Whoever pronounces a blessing in the earth[NOTE:1] will do so in the name of the faithful God;[NOTE:2] whoever makes an oath in the earthwill do so in the name of the faithful God.[NOTE:3] For past problems will be forgotten;I will no longer think about them.[NOTE:4]
notes: Or “in the land” (NIV, NCV, NRSV). The same phrase occurs again later in this verse, with the same options.
Heb “will pronounce a blessing by the God of truth.”
Heb “will take an oath by the God of truth.”
Heb “for the former distresses will be forgotten, and they will be hidden from my eyes.”

verses.zh: 看哪！我造新天新地；从前的事不再被记念，也不再追想。
verses.en: For look, I am ready to create new heavens and a new earth![NOTE:1] The former ones[NOTE:2] will not be remembered;no one will think about them anymore.[NOTE:3]
notes: This hyperbolic statement likens the coming transformation of Jerusalem (see vv. 18-19) to a new creation of the cosmos.
Or perhaps, “the former things” (so ASV, NASB, NIV, NRSV); TEV “The events of the past.”
Heb “and they will not come up on the mind.”

verses.zh: 你们当因我所造的永远欢喜快乐；因我造耶路撒冷为人所喜，造其中的居民为人所乐。
verses.en: But be happy and rejoice forevermoreover what I am about to create!For look, I am ready to create Jerusalem[NOTE:1] to be a source of joy,[NOTE:2] and her people to be a source of happiness.[NOTE:3]
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
Heb “Jerusalem, joy.” The next verse suggests the meaning: The Lord will create Jerusalem to be a source of joy to himself.
Heb “her people, happiness.” See the preceding note.

verses.zh: 我必因耶路撒冷欢喜，因我的百姓快乐；其中必不再听见哭泣的声音和哀号的声音。
verses.en: Jerusalem will bring me joy,and my people will bring me happiness.[NOTE:1] The sound of weeping or cries of sorrowwill never be heard in her again.
notes: Heb “and I will rejoice in Jerusalem and be happy in my people.”

verses.zh: 其中必没有数日夭亡的婴孩，也没有寿数不满的老者；因为百岁死的仍算孩童，有百岁死的罪人算被咒诅。
verses.en: Never again will one of her infants live just a few days[NOTE:1] or an old man die before his time.[NOTE:2] Indeed, no one will die before the age of one hundred;[NOTE:3] anyone who fails to reach[NOTE:4] the age of one hundred will be considered cursed.
notes: Heb “and there will not be from there again a nursing infant of days,” i.e., one that lives just a few days.
Heb “or an old [man] who does not fill out his days.”

Heb “for the child as a son of one hundred years will die.” The point seems to be that those who die at the age of a hundred will be considered children, for the average life span will be much longer than that. The category “child” will be redefined in light of the expanded life spans that will characterize this new era.

Heb “the one who misses.” חָטָא (khataʾ) is used here in its basic sense of “miss the mark.” See HALOT 305 s.v. חטא. Another option is to translate, “and the sinner who reaches the age of a hundred will be cursed.”

verses.zh: 他们要建造房屋，自己居住；栽种葡萄园，吃其中的果子。
verses.en: They will build houses and live in them;they will plant vineyards and eat their fruit.

verses.zh: 他们建造的，别人不得住；他们栽种的，别人不得吃；因为我民的日子必像树木的日子；我选民亲手劳碌得来的必长久享用。
verses.en: No longer will they build a house only to have another live in it,[NOTE:1] or plant a vineyard only to have another eat its fruit,[NOTE:2] for my people will live as long as trees,[NOTE:3] and my chosen ones will enjoy to the fullest what they have produced.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “they will not build, and another live [in it].”
Heb “they will not plant, and another eat.”
Heb “for like the days of the tree [will be] the days of my people.”
Heb “the work of their hands” (so KJV, NASB, NIV, NRSV); NLT “their hard-won gains.”

verses.zh: 他们必不徒然劳碌，所生产的，也不遭灾害，因为都是蒙耶和华赐福的后裔；他们的子孙也是如此。
verses.en: They will not work in vainor give birth to children that will experience disaster.[NOTE:1] For the Lord will bless their childrenand their descendants.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and they will not give birth to horror.”
Heb “for offspring blessed by the Lord they [will be], and their descendants along with them.”

verses.zh: 他们尚未求告，我就应允；正说话的时候，我就垂听。
verses.en: Before they even call out,[NOTE:1] I will respond;while they are still speaking, I will hear.
notes: The verb that introduces this verse serves as a discourse particle and is untranslated; see note on “in the future” in 2:2.

verses.zh: 豺狼必与羊羔同食；狮子必吃草与牛一样；尘土必作蛇的食物。在我圣山的遍处，这一切都不伤人，不害物。这是耶和华说的。
verses.en: A wolf and a lamb will graze together;[NOTE:1] a lion, like an ox, will eat straw,[NOTE:2] and a snake’s food will be dirt.[NOTE:3] They will no longer injure or destroyon my entire royal mountain,”[NOTE:4] says the Lord.
notes: A similar statement appears in 11:6.
These words also appear in 11:7.

Some see an allusion to Gen 3:14 (note “you will eat dirt”). The point would be that even in this new era the snake (often taken as a symbol of Satan) remains under God’s curse. However, it is unlikely that such an allusion exists. Even if there is an echo of Gen 3:14, the primary allusion is to 11:8, where snakes are pictured as no longer dangerous. They will no longer attack other living creatures, but will be content to crawl along the ground. (The statement “you will eat dirt” in Gen 3:14 means “you will crawl on the ground.” In the same way the statement “dirt will be its food” in Isa 65:25 means “it will crawl on the ground.”)

Heb “in all my holy mountain.” These same words appear in 11:9. See the note there.sn As in 11:1-9 the prophet anticipates a time when the categories predator-prey no longer exist. See the note at the end of 11:8.

READING CYCLE THREE (see
"Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- These last two chapters are contained in a literary unit which runs from Isaiah 56 to Isaiah 66. It could
be characterized as "A New Day" or "The New Age." See my new (2024) exegetical, verse-by-verse
commentary on Revelation 21-22, free online.

- OT prophets used contemporary occurrences to foreshadow future events. The return of the exiles
seems to be the foreshadowing of the spiritual return of all of God's human creation to an original
Adamic fellowship of Eden

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

SPECIAL TOPIC: PROPHECY (OT)

- Isaiah. 65 is possibly a response to Isaiah's corporate prayer for help and mercy which is recorded in
Isa. 63:7-64:12. God's basic answer is that He has always been ready (cf. Isa. 55:6-7), but His people
have always turned away from Him (Isa. 65:5).

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

- It is quite interesting that Paul uses Isa. 65:1-2 in Rom. 10:20-21. Paul interprets Isa. 65:1 as
referring to the Gentiles and Isa. 65:2 as referring to the Jews. In context they both seem to be
related to the returning Judeans of Ezra's and Nehemiah's day. However, Isa. 65:1d, which contains
the phrase, "to a nation which did not call on My name," could refer to the Jewish nation unless
it is used in some kind of idolatrous, sarcastic, ironical way.

- Isaiah 65 is also unique in prophecy because it takes the concept of corporality into the area of
individual response. The two groups can be clearly seen in Isa. 65:10c and 11a. God will make a
distinction within the nation between those who know Him and those who reject Him
(cf. Ezek. 18:1-21; 33:10-20; and Jer. 31:29-30.

- Isaiah 65 culminates Isaiah's unique emphasis on the universal love of God and its inclusion of
the Gentiles (i.e. Isa. 2:2-4; 12:4-5; 25:6-9; 42:6-12; 45:22-23; 49:5-6; 51:4-5; 56:7; 60:1,3; 66:23). He
goes so far as to say that God will even make some Gentiles priests and Levites (cf. Isa. 61:6; 66:21). This
is very significant in light of the obvious conclusions of Jewish monotheism and the call of Abraham
in Gen. 12:1-3, which also included all of the world (i.e. Exod. 19:5-6).

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

- It is surprising that this New Age is described without any allusions to the Messiah of Isaiah 9 and 11.

- For a good brief discussion of ANE views of the afterlife, see John H. Walton, ANE Thought and the OT, pp. 314-329.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: ISAIAH 65:1-7

1"I permitted Myself to be sought by those who did not ask

for Me;

I permitted Myself to be found by those who did not seek Me.

I said, 'Here am I, here am I,'

To a nation which did not call on My name.

2I have spread out My hands all day long to a rebellious

people,

Who walk in the way which is not good, following their own

thoughts,

3A people who continually provoke Me to My face,

Offering sacrifices in gardens and burning incense

on bricks;

4Who sit among graves and spend the night in secret places;

Who eat swine's flesh,

And the broth of unclean meat is in their pots.

5Who say, 'Keep to yourself, do not come near me,

For I am holier than you!'

These are smoke in My nostrils,

A fire that burns all the day.

6Behold, it is written before Me,

I will not keep silent, but I will repay;

I will even repay into their bosom,

7Both their own iniquities and the iniquities of their fathers together,"

says the Lord.

"Because they have burned incense on the mountains

And scorned Me on the hills,

Therefore I will measure their former work into their bosom."

65:2 "I permitted Myself to be sought. . .to be found" God always takes the initiative in spiritual
matters (i.e. John 6:44,65). Humans are only responders in the spiritual realm, not initiators! Even in this
context He is allowing Himself to be found, revealing Himself to the children of Abraham and to the
other children of Adam (cf. Isa. 55:6-7; John 10:16; see SPECIAL TOPIC: Seek the Lord).
These opening verses remind me of Romans 11.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WAYS OF REVELATION

▣ "Here am I, here am I" The doubling is for emphasis! These are words of a Hebrew idiom of
availability (i.e. Isa. 6:8; 52:6). God was always available but His people would not respond ("ask," "seek").

▣ "To a nation which did not call on My name" In context this refers either to

- the covenant people who called upon idols, particularly the fertility gods

- the Gentiles (cf. Rom. 10:20-21)

The concept of calling upon someone's name is the idea of responding to them in a worship setting. Paul
uses this same concept of calling upon the name of the Lord in Rom. 10:9-13 (cf. Acts 7:59; 9:14,21; 22:16;
1 Cor. 1:2; 2 Tim. 2:22; see SPECIAL TOPIC: The Name of the Lord [NT]).
This was considered an act of trust and worship.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CALL ON HIS NAME

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH

65:2 "I spread out My hands all day long to a rebellious people" This is anthropomorphic imagery
which shows the intensity and openness of God's love (cf. Rom. 10:21). Usually it is a gesture of prayer but here of welcome.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PROBLEMS AND LIMITATIONS OF HUMAN LANGUAGE

SPECIAL TOPIC: STUBBORNNESS (OT)

▣ "Who walk in the way which is not good, following their own thoughts" The following
verses list several aspects of idolatry which characterize the covenant people. It is very difficult in this period of
history to completely understand each one of these aspects in detail (cf. Isa. 65:3-7). Some say that they are all
caught up in the garden worship mentioned in Isa. 65:3, while others differentiate between the groups. What is
obvious is that God's people had turned to other gods. Some possible enumerations of these idolatrous traits are

- offering sacrifice in gardens

- burning incense on bricks

- sitting among graves

- spending nights in secret places

- eating swine's flesh

- having the broth of unclean meat in their pots

- burning incense on mountains

- scorning Me on the hills

- setting a table for "Fortune," Isa. 65:11

- filling cups of mixed wine for "Destiny"

65:3 "A people who continually provoke Me to My face" This is Hebrew imagery of repeated,
open defiance to God. Sin is primarily against God (cf. 2 Sam. 12:13; Ps. 41:4; 51:4; also note Gen. 20:6; 39:9).
Idolatry had become so common and accepted that it was not even hidden.

SPECIAL TOPIC: IDOLATRY

SPECIAL TOPIC: MAGIC

▣ "Offering sacrifice in gardens" We are not sure if this is

- the ancient veneration of trees that can be seen in Isa. 1:29; Hosea 4:13 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: TREES)

- a particularized worship within a garden setting (cf. Isa. 66:17)

▣ "burning incense on bricks" It has been suggested that the term "bricks" can simply refer to

- an altar made with cut stones (cf. Lev. 20:24-25)

- the pillars of Ba'al worship (cf. Lev. 26:1)

- the roof tiles which relate to the worship of Babylonian astral deities

- incense altars (see IVP Bible Background Commentary: OT, p. 640)

These numerous possibilities show us that we simply do not know what this really means.

65:4 "Who sit among graves" This seems to be some kind of worship or communication with the dead,
possibly necromancy or ancestral worship (cf. Lev. 19:31; 20:6,27; Deut. 18:10-12).

SPECIAL TOPIC: MAGIC

The MT has the VERBAL "watch," "guard," or
"keep" (BDB 665 I, #4, KB 718, Qal PASSIVE PARTICIPLE). It can denote

- a city besieged ‒ Isa. 1:8

- YHWH is Israel's keeper ‒ Isa. 27:3

- YHWH keeps Israel ‒ Isa. 42:6

- YHWH declares hidden things ‒ Isa. 48:6

- YHWH preserves Israel ‒ Isa. 49:6

- YHWH will keep Israel ‒ Isa. 49:8

The best parallel seems to be #4. If so, then REB is the best understanding of the VERBAL.

We really do not have any idea what this has reference to but it seems to involve the cultic arts in some way.

- necromancy

- ancestor worship

▣ "Who eat swine's flesh,

And the broth of unclean meat is in their pots" Usually these two acts are
connected by commentators although this is uncertain. They are a violation of the food laws of Leviticus 11
(cf. Isa. 11:7). Pigs were common sacrifices of the surrounding nations (i.e. Ugaritic Texts).

The MT has "fragment," פרק, BDB 830, but BDB suggests
(Qere) מרק, BDB 600 II, "a rich broth," along with DSS, LXX, and Aramaic Targum.

65:8 "As the new wine is found in the cluster" This is imagery that even in a cluster
of good grapes there are always some bad grapes. This is the beginning of a discussion that runs from Isa. 65:8 to
Isa. 65:10 which states that a remnant of the covenant people will be faithful to YHWH. However, Isa. 65:11-13
shows the complete rejection and judgment of those of Judah who continue to reject YHWH by covenant disobedience and
idolatry. This is the beginning of the painful but true emphasis that judgment will begin with the house of God (cf. 1 Pet. 4:17).
There is a form of OT religion in which God takes no pleasure. God looks at the heart (cf. Isa. 29:13).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE REMNANT, THREE SENSES

SPECIAL TOPIC: BIBLICAL ATTITUDES TOWARD ALCOHOL AND ALCOHOL ABUSE

65:10-11 "For My people who seek Me.

But you who forsake the Lord" This verse highlights the
individual aspect of the covenant of Moses. YHWH had always dealt in a corporate aspect with the nation. The
entire nation was blessed or the entire nation was cursed (i.e. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28-29). Now we are
coming to the individualized focus of Ezek. 18:32; 30:10-19; and Jer. 31:29-30, where there is a distinction within
the people of God as to those who believe and those who do not believe (cf. Deut. 29:24-28). Later in Isaiah 66 there
will be a distinction between all mankind, of those who reject and those who receive YHWH.

(Qal PARTICIPLE, BDB 736 I, KB 806) means "to abandon" or "to leave." It is regularly

"cups" are sacrificial imagery of the ANE theology of the necessity of feeding the gods. This imagery is never used

65:17 "For behold, I create new heavens and a new earth" The context of Isa. 65:17-25 is extremely
important because it is the key, not only of these last two chapters, but of God making all things new
(cf. Isa. 42:9; 48:6; 66:22; 2 Pet. 3:13; Rev. 21-22). It is a discussion of the New Age or the Age of the Messiah
(cf. Rom. 8:18-25). It also implies that the current order will be destroyed (cf. Isa. 51:6 and 2 Pet. 3:10). There
is also a relation between Isa. 65:16 and 17 that the New Order will not contain sins because they will be
forgiven, as is mentioned in the latter part of Isa. 65:16.

The terminology of "a new heaven and a new earth" is common in Jewish Apocalyptic
Literature (cf. II Esdras 6:11-24; I Enoch 91:16). This becomes the imagery for Revelation 21-22! The earth will
return to its pre-Genesis 3 glory and purpose. See full note at Isa. 62:2 and my new Partial Preterist commentary on the
book of Revelation, online.

For a good discussion on the biblical material about earthly Jerusalem and heavenly Jerusalem, see
Dale Moody, The Word of Truth, pp. 569-588.

or the planet. Only context can determine which one. It is obvious in the phrase, "new heaven and new earth," that it
denotes the whole planet.

▣ "forever" This term (BDB 723 I) denotes perpetual fellowship with the Creator and His
human vessels (cf. 1 Chr. 28:9; Micah 7:18). There is a Hebrew sound play between the PREPOSITION
(BDB 723 III) and the NOUN "forever" (BDB 723 I), which denotes perpetuity.

65:19 "And there will no longer be heard in her

The voice of weeping and the sound of crying" This is the continual theme of Isaiah
that the New Age will not have the pain of this former sin-cursed earth (cf. Isa. 25:8; 30:19; 35:10; 51:11). This
seems to be alluded to in Rev. 7:17 and 21:4.

65:20 "No longer will there be in it an infant who lives but

a few days,

Or an old man who does not live out his days" This hyperbolic statement can have one of two origins.

- an allusion to the long lives of Genesis 1-5, thereby denoting a return to the Garden of Eden period

- an OT way of describing the "New Age," which we know from the NT involves not just protracted physical
life (i.e. the OT view of an afterlife), but a new eternal life (zoa)

For a good discussion of Isaiah's discussion of extended lives and the NT discussion of eternal life,
see Hard Sayings of the Bible, pp. 307-309.

65:22 This is imagery to describe the fact that the people will live in the land and enjoy its fruits. It is a
direct allusion to the exile and the promise of a return to Palestine.

Revelation 21-22, a restored Garden of Eden). It will be as it was!
